name: study2-checkpoint-2.1-cuda-validation

rest.note: v2 field names. The previous body used v1/GraphQL names (gpuType, gpuCount, cloudType, containerDiskInGb, volumeInGb) and had no image, which v2 requires.

networkVolume.note: No network volume or paid storage. The pod downloads the pinned Qwen files to its container disk and checks every sha256 against docker/cuda/qwen_files.sha256 before measuring.

image.registry: ghcr.io (public package, so no registry credential)

weights.source: Hugging Face Qwen/Qwen3-VL-2B-Instruct, revision 89644892e4d85e24eaac8bacfd4f463576704203, license apache-2.0, not gated

resultExport: Pod log stream only. Sections are delimited by '=== BEGIN <file>' and '=== END <file>'. The terminal job line is exactly one of '=== JOB_DONE status=ok' or '=== JOB_FAILED step=<s> rc=<n> reason=<r>'. Only JOB_DONE status=ok is a usable result. docker/runpod/capture_logs.sh saves the stream on the operator machine; the job then waits JOB_RESULT_GRACE_SECONDS (120) before stopping itself. RunPod does not document that pod logs outlive termination.

shutdown.inPod: Every step runs under timeout against JOB_DEADLINE_MINUTES (45). A watchdog calls self_stop.py 5 minutes after that. After the terminal line and the 120 s result grace, self_stop.py asks REST v2 to stop the pod, then to terminate it, with the pod-scoped RUNPOD_API_KEY. If both are refused it prints SELF_STOP_FAILED and sleeps instead of exiting, so the container never reruns the job.
shutdown.whyStopFirst: The pod has no volume mount, and RunPod does not bill a stopped pod's container disk, so a stopped pod costs $0. Stopping keeps the pod record (and its log) for the operator, who terminates it after the log is saved.
shutdown.operator: Right after create, start docker/runpod/capture_logs.sh <pod-id> <file> and docker/runpod/deadline_guard.sh <pod-id> 60. The guard terminates that pod id at 60 minutes.
shutdown.accountCap: The prepaid balance is the hard ceiling: at $0 RunPod stops all pods, and pods without a network volume are terminated. RunPod requires one hour of credit to create the pod (about $0.59 here). The account spend limit ($80/h by default) is not a useful cap at this scale.
shutdown.notAvailable: REST v2 has no stop timer. runpodctl --stop-after/--terminate-after are not relied on (see CUDA_VALIDATION.md).
shutdown.documented: In-pod stop: RunPod documents `runpodctl pod stop $RUNPOD_POD_ID` from inside the pod (docs.runpod.io/pods/manage-pods).
shutdown.unverified: Whether the pod-scoped key may call the REST v2 action route (stop or terminate) has not been checked on a live pod. If it is refused, the deadline guard and the balance cap remain.

estimatedCostUsd.expectedMinutes: 15-30 including image pull and the 4.3 GB weight download
